pr.title: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes

raw_findings.body: The link no longer preserves the previous 30% primary-lightness appearance in light themes and uses the wrong secondary lightness in dark themes, producing unintended contrast and emphasis.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Generated topic metadata CSS uses the wrong color branch in both theme modes.
raw_findings.impact: The link no longer preserves the previous 30% primary-lightness appearance in light themes and uses the wrong secondary lightness in dark themes, producing unintended contrast and emphasis.
raw_findings.root_cause: The migration swapped the original lightness values instead of preserving the primary value and complementing it for the secondary branch.
raw_findings.title: Topic metadata links use swapped lightness values
raw_findings.trigger: Render the topic metadata author link in a light or dark color scheme.

raw_findings.body: The custom message length hint changes from the original 70% primary-lightness to 30% in light themes, and selects 70% secondary-lightness instead of 30% in dark themes, making the hint visibly mis-emphasized.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The mobile modal renders its secondary hint with the wrong contrast in both theme modes.
raw_findings.impact: The custom message length hint changes from the original 70% primary-lightness to 30% in light themes, and selects 70% secondary-lightness instead of 30% in dark themes, making the hint visibly mis-emphasized.
raw_findings.root_cause: The replacement reversed the original lightness values during the dark-theme conversion.
raw_findings.title: Mobile flag message hint reverses the intended lightness
raw_findings.trigger: Open the flag modal on a mobile viewport with either a light or dark color scheme.

raw_findings.body: The `h3` heading changes from the original 20% primary-lightness to 50% in light themes and from the expected 80% secondary-lightness to 50% in dark themes, weakening the intended heading hierarchy.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Topic-map headings render with an unintended muted color on mobile.
raw_findings.impact: The `h3` heading changes from the original 20% primary-lightness to 50% in light themes and from the expected 80% secondary-lightness to 50% in dark themes, weakening the intended heading hierarchy.
raw_findings.root_cause: The migration substituted a 50/50 pair instead of retaining the source declaration's 20% light-theme value and complementary dark-theme value.
raw_findings.title: Mobile topic-map headings lose their original emphasis
raw_findings.trigger: Expand the topic map on a mobile device in either theme mode.

raw_findings.body: Member names use the 50/50 color pair instead of the original 30% primary-lightness and its 70% dark-theme counterpart, reducing the intended distinction and contrast.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Desktop group member names are styled like mid-level metadata rather than the darker name text defined before the patch.
raw_findings.impact: Member names use the 50/50 color pair instead of the original 30% primary-lightness and its 70% dark-theme counterpart, reducing the intended distinction and contrast.
raw_findings.root_cause: The color conversion changed the original name-specific lightness to the generic 50/50 pair.
raw_findings.title: Desktop group member names use the wrong color level
raw_findings.trigger: Render the group member information section on a desktop user page.

raw_findings.body: Member names use the 50/50 color pair instead of the original 30% primary-lightness and its 70% dark-theme counterpart, causing unintended text contrast and hierarchy on mobile.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Mobile group member names render with the wrong emphasis in both theme modes.
raw_findings.impact: Member names use the 50/50 color pair instead of the original 30% primary-lightness and its 70% dark-theme counterpart, causing unintended text contrast and hierarchy on mobile.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mobile counterpart of the group-member name rule was converted to a generic 50/50 pair rather than preserving its original 30% lightness.
raw_findings.title: Mobile group member names use the wrong color level
raw_findings.trigger: Render group member information on a mobile user page.

raw_findings.body: The comment still states that the default is only `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, omitting that the migrated rules now select a secondary-based result for dark themes and misleading future color adjustments.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Code review and future maintenance rely on an incomplete description of the color behavior.
raw_findings.impact: The comment still states that the default is only `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, omitting that the migrated rules now select a secondary-based result for dark themes and misleading future color adjustments.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch changed the theme-dependent implementation without updating the explanatory comment immediately above it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment to document the `dark-light-choose` light-theme and dark-theme results, including the 50/50 low-level default.
raw_findings.title: Coldmap documentation no longer describes the dark-theme behavior
raw_findings.trigger: A maintainer uses the adjacent coldmap comment to reason about default topic-list cell colors for a dark color scheme.

raw_findings.body: CI can accept a visually incorrect theme conversion such as this swapped 70/30 mapping because compilation alone does not verify preservation of the original light-theme result or the intended dark-theme fallback.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Wrong lightness pairs reach production undetected despite passing asset compilation.
raw_findings.impact: CI can accept a visually incorrect theme conversion such as this swapped 70/30 mapping because compilation alone does not verify preservation of the original light-theme result or the intended dark-theme fallback.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces many theme-dependent color transformations without coverage for their branch-specific output.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a Sass stylesheet test or generated-CSS fixture that evaluates each migrated selector with light and dark `$primary`/`$secondary` values and asserts that the light branch preserves the old `scale-color($primary, ...)` result while the dark branch uses the specified secondary lightness.
raw_findings.title: No regression test protects the migrated light/dark color mapping
raw_findings.trigger: A future mass replacement changes one branch's lightness while the stylesheet still compiles successfully.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a Sass stylesheet test or generated-CSS fixture that evaluates each migrated selector with light and dark `$primary`/`$secondary` values and asserts that the light branch preserves the old `scale-color($primary, ...)` result while the dark branch uses the specified secondary lightness.
validated_findings.title: No regression test protects the migrated light/dark color mapping
validated_findings.trigger: A future mass replacement changes one branch's lightness while the stylesheet still compiles successfully.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test gap suggestion, not a concrete bug. The claim that CI 'can accept visually incorrect theme conversion' is speculative and assumes the conversions are incorrect, which is unverified. Absence of visual regression tests is a general observation, not a defect introduced by this patch.
